findings.title: Write gate validates the pre-serialization object; caller code at the final stringify can diverge the written bytes from the gate-validated candidate
findings.recommendation: The iter-4 fix closed the trail-DIRECTORY half of the check/use seam (serialize, then re-run assertCanonicalTrailDir before the write) but not the content half: writeGate runs at :1041 against the live emit object, and the final JSON.stringify at :1047 then re-reads caller-supplied nested values (property getters, toJSON hooks on findings/scorecard/resolutions/handoff entries — the exact in-process vector the accepted iter-4 reproduction and the new regression test both use). A nested object can present gate-clean values to normalizeInternalPass/scorecardRollupCheck and serialize different ones — e.g. a finding title that is single-line at gate time and carries an embedded newline in the written bytes — defeating the 'a malformed emit is refused before it becomes a record' write-time guarantee (read-side render validation and orientation's spine-invalid skip remain as defense-in-depth, which is why this is WARNING, not CRITICAL). Fix by the same pattern already applied for the trail dir: serialize first, then run writeGate against JSON.parse(serialized) (the frozen bytes ARE the validated candidate), then the canonical-trail re-check, then write; extend the toctou regression with a toJSON hook that forges a gate-checked slot and prove the write refuses.

findings.title: Doc-scoped address-reviews iteration counts every doc's walk logs on the shared architecture trail — no per-doc anchoring
findings.recommendation: The address-reviews iteration is computed as the count of ALL prior address-reviews-*.json in resolved.runsDir + 1. For --doc walks the runsDir is the SHARED orbit/architecture/.orbit-runs/, so a walk on doc B counts doc A's logs in its ordinal — the exact cross-doc anchoring the review-architecture ordinal deliberately avoids (prior emits filtered by matching doc, per the same file's :818-:827 and orbit-review's per-doc rule). The delta's wording ('the count of prior address-reviews emits on the change's trail plus one') doesn't resolve the shared-trail case. Filter doc-scoped walk logs by matching doc field (mirroring the review-architecture ordinal) and state the per-doc rule in the delta's address-reviews iteration sentence.

findings.title: config.yaml models-hint comment omits `fresh` from the cadence-slot key list the gates delta defines
findings.recommendation: The commented guidance reads 'cadence slot names (in-context, independent, external)' while the orbit-engine-gates delta (and model-hints.ts's own doc comment) define FOUR slot keys: in-context, fresh, independent, external. A user configuring a `fresh:` hint from the config comment alone wouldn't know the key exists (the engine honors it). Align the comment with the delta's two vocabularies; while there, confirm `archive` genuinely resolves as a phase key for next_hint_keys or drop it from the phase-id example list.

commentary: A later fresh pass over a heavily-converged state: four external iterations plus three internal confirms have already sanded most of this change, so I aimed the depth at the one surface that moved since the last clean confirm — the uncommitted serialize-then-recheck fix — and re-derived the verification facts independently rather than trusting the trail (build, full suite, strict validation, fingerprints, the 15+15 generated surface, live boot/touchpoints arithmetic, apply-emit consent fields, architecture stage states). The pattern in what remains is instructive: the iter-4 fix is correct for exactly the vector its regression names, but the same vector has a second half — the write gate's validated candidate and the written bytes are still two different reads of caller-influenced state, and the fix itself demonstrates the closing pattern one call earlier. The other residues are edge-vocabulary nits (a shared-trail ordinal, a config comment lagging the delta's key list) of the kind that only surface when reading the current bytes with no memory of how they got there. The disciplines held: every prior-cycle finding I checked was genuinely closed on disk, several with wording upgrades beyond the minimum, which is what a trail this long should buy.
